description: University-endorsed, free for all students; described as the go-to option for students' AI needs and usable with public and protected information (only some highly protected data). Assessment use still depends on the unit outline.
howToObtain: Sign in with your University account via Okta.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Microsoft Copilot is a University endorsed GenAI tool and is free for all students. You're welcome to use it for assessments provided you are aware of how to use AI tools responsibly.

The go-to option for students' AI needs. Microsoft Copilot Chat is secure, supported, and ready to use with public and protected information (but only some highly protected data).
For data protection, always sign in with your University account via Okta.

description: University-built teaching AI platform designed by Sydney educators; students use agents provided in their units.
howToObtain: Through units where educators provide Cogniti agents.
costToUser: Not stated in the reviewed sources.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Designed by University of Sydney educators, Cogniti assists student learning in interactive and context-sensitive ways.

description: Legal-specialist AI tool available to all Sydney Law School students (faculty-specific, not university-wide).
howToObtain: Sydney Law School students; see the Law School FAQs.
costToUser: Not stated in the reviewed sources.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: All University of Sydney Law School students have access to Harvey AI, a legal-specialist AI tool used across the profession.

description: Planned institution-wide tool: student pilot planned for October 2026, release to all students scheduled for Semester 1 2027. Agents, plugins and connectors assessed individually before enabling. Australian data residency at rest, globally routed inference.
howToObtain: Not yet generally available to students; University single sign-on once released.
costToUser: Not stated as a student charge; University cost is commercial in confidence.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: A student pilot of ChatGPT Edu is planned for October 2026, around the time of the staff release of the tool. Following the pilot, ChatGPT Edu is scheduled for release to all students in Semester 1 2027.
Additional capabilities such as custom GPTs, agents, plugins, connectors and other advanced features will be individually assessed before being enabled.
The University of Sydney's ChatGPT Edu workspace has Australian data residency at rest and globally routed inference.
